# Summary of Recommended Fixes Across Quarterly Incident Reports

## Executive summary
Only three fixes are explicitly recommended across the Q1–Q3 2024 incident reports. All three are in the Q2 postmortem: automate database volume expansion, review rate limit changes before deployment, and run quarterly failover drills. Disk-full database outages still recurred in all three quarters (Q1 240 min, Q2 180 min, Q3 120 min). The Q3 outage happened after the automation fix was proposed. Many root causes have no recorded remediation, including connection pool exhaustion, the expired TLS certificate and the third-party gateway outage. The sources don't show whether any recommended action was completed.

## Findings
### Explicit recommended fixes (Q2 postmortem)
The Q2 postmortem lists three actions: automate database volume expansion, review rate limit changes before deployment, and run quarterly failover drills. Reviewing rate limit changes addresses the misconfigured rate limit in INC-201. Automating volume expansion is the only recommended fix aimed at the recurring disk-full database outages. [S2] [S8]

### Recurring disk-full database outages
Disk-full database outages occurred in Q1 (INC-101, 240 min), Q2 (INC-202, 180 min) and Q3 (INC-302, 120 min). The Q3 narrative calls the August outage the same class of failure as the two earlier database outages. This suggests earlier remediation was not effective or not implemented in time. ### Monitoring gap for disk usage
The Q1 narrative notes that no disk usage alert existed when the primary volume reached 100%. This is a stated gap, not an explicit recommendation. The sources do not show that an alert was added afterwards. [S10]

### Reactive fixes with no preventive action
The Q3 search index corruption was fixed by rebuilding the index. The Q3 payments outage was a third-party gateway failure that the report calls outside the organisation's control. No preventive action is recorded for either. [S4] [S1]

### Root causes with no recorded remediation
Connection pool exhaustion (Q1 payments INC-102 and Q2 checkout INC-203) and the expired TLS certificate that nobody was assigned to renew (Q1 INC-103) are described, but no corrective actions are listed. [S10] [S3] [S8]

## Recommendations
- Confirm the status of the Q2 action "Automate database volume expansion" and treat it as a priority, since the disk-full failure recurred in Q3 after it was proposed.
- Consider adding disk usage alerting, because the Q1 narrative identifies its absence as a gap.
- Define corrective actions for connection pool exhaustion, which caused two incidents (INC-102 and INC-203).
- Assign an owner for TLS certificate renewal, since the Q1 expiry happened because nobody was assigned to renew it.
- Record preventive actions for incidents that were only fixed reactively, such as the Q3 search index corruption.
- Evaluate options for the third-party payment gateway dependency, because the Q3 outage had no recorded follow-up action.
- Record an owner, deadline and completion status for every postmortem action.
